Simulate detections of transmissions by a receiver array

simulate_detections.Rd

Draws, for every transmission and every receiver in a detection field, one Bernoulli trial with the detection probability the field gives that receiver at the cell holding the transmission. The field is a de_field from detfield::de_field(): eta, a matrix of cells by receivers on the logit scale; cells, the water-cell ids of its rows; receivers, the receiver keys of its columns; key, the column the keys come from; and grid, the raster template the cell ids refer to. A list of the same shape with no key is read as keyed by receiver_serial.

Usage

simulate_detections(
  transmissions,
  field,
  overdispersion = c("station_hour", "none"),
  min_cover = 0.5,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

transmissions

A sim_transmissions object from simulate_transmissions().

field

A de_field: see Details.

overdispersion

"station_hour" (default) or "none"; see Details.

min_cover

Share of a UTC hour, from 0 to 1, that a station's deployments must cover for it to listen in the hour; the default is the default of detfield::bin_detections(). Used only when the field's lookup has deployment times; see Details.

seed

Seed; NULL uses the current random number stream. The caller's stream is restored after a seeded call. The draws depend on the generator kind as well as the seed; the kind is stored with the result. Without overdispersion, transmission i always takes the i-th run of uniform numbers, one per receiver, so the first m transmissions get the same draws whether they are simulated alone or with more. With it, the hourly effects are drawn first, one run per hour in time order, and the uniform numbers follow, hour by hour. Trials of a station not listening are drawn and then discarded, so they do not change the other draws.

Value

A list of class sim_detections with two data frames: detections, one row per detection, with the columns of the positionR table contract (datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter, animal_id, and station_id when the field is keyed by station) and transmission_id, ordered by time and receiver key; and transmissions, the truth: every transmission with its position, heard or not, and n_detections, the receivers that heard it. Attributes: seed, rng_kind (the RNGkind() in force), overdispersion, station_hour, the standard deviation used (0 for none), and trials_not_listening, the transmission and station trials not made because the station was not listening (0 when none were left out).

Details

Receivers and stations. A field built from a table with a station_id column has stations as its columns. The detections then carry station_id, and receiver_serial is the receiver deployed at that station at the time of the detection, read from the field's lookup (the deployments given to detfield::water_distances()). Where two deployments of a station overlap, the receiver deployed later takes the detection, as in detfield::bin_detections(). With no lookup, receiver_serial is NA, and detfield::bin_detections() matches the detections by station to listening rows that have no serial.

Stations not listening. When the lookup has deployment times, a station makes a trial only when it listens, by the rule of detfield::bin_detections() with hour bins: a receiver is in the water at the station at the time of the transmission, and the station's deployments together cover at least min_cover of that UTC hour. A station deployed late, recovered early or between receivers therefore makes no detection at those times, and the detections that remain all fall in listening rows of detfield::bin_detections() given the same deployments and min_cover. A message gives the number of trials not made. A lookup with no times takes every station as listening throughout.

Overdispersion. With overdispersion = "station_hour", the default, each receiver and UTC hour gets one logit-scale effect, normal with standard deviation field$model$sigma$station_hour and shared by every animal in the hour: the form detfield::location_surface() integrates. When the field's model has no such value (NA, absent, or 0), or with "none", the trials are independent binomial draws. Left at its default with a spread above 0, the call says so in a message.

The function stops when a transmission falls on a cell the field does not hold, or when any detection probability it needs is missing. It never fills a gap with a guessed probability, because a guess would be scored as if the range model had predicted it.

See also

simulate_transmissions(), coverage_summary()

Examples

stoney <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                  package = "arraydesign"))
planned <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "planned_stations.csv",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
rx <- place_receivers(stoney, method = "manual", coords = planned)
# A deployments table: one receiver per station for two days.
deployments <- data.frame(
  receiver_serial = rx$receiver_serial, station_id = rx$station_id,
  x = rx$x, y = rx$y, deploy_z = rx$deploy_z,
  deploy_datetime = as.POSIXct("2024-12-31", tz = "UTC"),
  recover_datetime = as.POSIXct("2025-01-02", tz = "UTC")
)
range_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                     depth = c(1, 35))
# Pairs more than 4 km apart through water are left out. At the deepest
# receiver the curve gives them a detection probability below 1e-7, and
# the distances take a third of the time.
field <- detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(stoney, deployments,
                                                    max_distance = 4000),
                            range_model)
#> 52 of 2,304 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.

# Five tracks of 2 hours.
tr <- simulate_tracks(stoney, crw_model(30, 15, 40, time_step_s = 60),
                      n_animals = 5, n_steps = 120, seed = 1)
tx <- simulate_transmissions(tr, tag_delay = c(120, 180), seed = 2)
# This range model has no station-hour effect. Each detection probability
# comes from the range curve alone, with no random effect per receiver or
# hour.
det <- simulate_detections(tx, field, overdispersion = "none", seed = 3)
head(det$detections)
#>              datetime receiver_serial station_id transmitter animal_id
#> 1 2025-01-01 00:07:26            R001       S001    SIM-0002         2
#> 2 2025-01-01 00:17:23            R017       S017    SIM-0001         1
#> 3 2025-01-01 00:21:17            R001       S001    SIM-0002         2
#> 4 2025-01-01 00:32:48            R017       S017    SIM-0001         1
#> 5 2025-01-01 00:37:55            R001       S001    SIM-0002         2
#> 6 2025-01-01 00:42:53            R001       S001    SIM-0002         2
#>   transmission_id
#> 1              51
#> 2               7
#> 3              57
#> 4              13
#> 5              64
#> 6              66
table(det$transmissions$n_detections)
#> 
#>   0   1 
#> 223  19 

# The detections go straight into detfield.
counts <- detfield::bin_detections(det$detections, deployments,
                                   tag_delay = c(120, 180))
table(counts$listening)
#> 
#> TRUE 
#>  100
